speaker: Unknown
en: Trailer
zh: 预告

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Now people are using AI in ways that aren't very great. So what's your take on that?
zh: 现在人们使用 AI 的方式并不太好。所以你对此怎么看?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: If you lack ideas and you're relying heavily on AI for everything, you're not really going to be that important.
zh: 如果你缺乏想法,并且事事都严重依赖 AI,那你其实不会那么重要。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Faisal Masud, SVP and President of HP. I wonder if you've found ways to achieve quality without getting through the nitty-gritty of some slop along the way?
zh: Faisal Masud,HP 高级副总裁兼总裁。我想知道你是否找到了不用经历一路上的那些垃圾内容就能达到高质量的方法?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: It's literally becoming hard to understand what's actually written by a human versus pure slop. In some cases, they're adding more work, not actually deducting.
zh: 现在要分辨哪些是真正由人写的、哪些是纯粹的垃圾内容,真的变得很难了。在某些情况下,它们反而增加了更多工作,而不是真正减少工作。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: The million-dollar question, for a lot of the CIOs being pitched software, hardware, hybrid solutions: how close are you to the outcome?
zh: 对于许多被推销软件、硬件、混合解决方案的 CIO 来说,那个价值百万美元的问题是:你离结果有多近?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: If we can't provide that return on their investment, we shouldn't exist. It's as simple as that.
zh: 如果我们不能为他们的投资提供回报,我们就不应该存在。就这么简单。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: The problem we're creating on the back end of all of this is: who's going to manage this fleet of agents?
zh: 我们在这一切的后端正在制造的问题是:谁来管理这支智能体舰队?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: So I think the flip is... Introduction
zh: 所以我认为反转是……引言

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Hey, this is Carlos, CEO at Product School and your host on The Product Podcast. My guest today is Faisal Masud, SVP and President of HP Digital Services, which is HP's software business. His path there is odd in the best way: six years at Amazon, then eBay, Groupon, CTO at Staples, then COO at Wing, Alphabet's drone-delivery moonshot, then CEO of Fabric. Now he runs software inside a company most people still think of as printers, and his platform tells customers to buy less hardware. Things we'll cover in this episode: the irony of the AI manifesto and the slop it produced; AI is part of your strategy, it cannot be the strategy; selling a product that tells HP customers to buy fewer HP machines; outcome-based pricing when you have fewer human seats to charge for; and why the middle-management layer is the one AI actually removes. Let's get into it. Welcome to The Product Podcast, Faisal.
zh: 嘿,我是 Carlos,Product School 的 CEO,也是 The Product Podcast 的主持人。我今天的嘉宾是 Faisal Masud,HP Digital Services 的高级副总裁兼总裁,这是 HP 的软件业务。他走到这一步的路径以一种最好的方式显得不同寻常:在 Amazon 待了六年,然后是 eBay、Groupon,Staples 的 CTO,然后是 Wing 的 COO——Alphabet 的无人机送货登月项目,然后是 Fabric 的 CEO。现在他在一家大多数人仍然认为是做打印机的公司里运营软件业务,而他的平台告诉客户少买硬件。本期节目我们会聊到:AI 宣言的讽刺性以及它产生的垃圾内容;AI 是你战略的一部分,它不能成为战略本身;销售一款告诉 HP 客户少买 HP 机器的产品;在人类席位越来越少的情况下采用基于结果的定价;以及为什么中层管理才是 AI 真正消除的那一层。让我们开始吧。欢迎来到 The Product Podcast,Faisal。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Nice to meet you. Understanding the Title, and Why HP Built a Software Business
zh: 很高兴见到你。理解头衔,以及 HP 为何建立软件业务

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Your title is very complicated, so you have to help me here. It says President and SVP of HP Digital Services.
zh: 你的头衔非常复杂,所以你得帮帮我。上面写着 HP Digital Services 总裁兼高级副总裁。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: That's right. I didn't create the title, but it's the internal title for, basically, running all of HP's commercial software business. So the digital part is essentially anything to do with software that we sell into our enterprises and channel partners.
zh: 没错。这个头衔不是我起的,但它是内部的头衔,基本上就是负责运营 HP 全部的商业软件业务。所以「数字」这部分本质上就是指我们销售给企业和渠道合作伙伴的一切软件相关的东西。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: That's kind of unique to HP. The first thing someone thinks of with HP is hardware, printers, right? So what was the rationale behind expanding into software as a service?
zh: 这在 HP 有点独特。提到 HP,人们首先想到的是硬件、打印机,对吧?那么扩展到软件即服务背后的考量是什么?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Back when I joined, around that time they were forming an organization that later became Digital Services. It was primarily set up to be exactly that: a bit of a deviation away from the hardware, the separation on purpose, so it could be a standalone operating unit that builds software to support the hardware business. The reason we did it is that it's very hard to just run a purely analog hardware business. You have to have the data around the hardware, and the thesis I've been building with the team has been exactly that: collect telemetry from what we serve our customers with, and then turn those insights back into serving our customers. From E-commerce and Drones to SaaS
zh: 我加入的时候,大约在那时他们正在组建一个后来成为 Digital Services 的组织。它的设立初衷正是如此:有意与硬件业务有所偏离、有所分离,这样它可以成为一个独立的运营单元,构建支持硬件业务的软件。我们这么做的原因是,纯粹运营一个模拟的硬件业务非常困难。你必须拥有硬件相关的数据,而我一直与团队构建的论点正是如此:从我们服务客户的设备中收集遥测数据,然后把这些洞察转化回服务客户。从电商和无人机到 SaaS

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: I was looking at your background. You worked at Amazon, eBay, Google, but the drone-delivery business, Wing, was also really cool. So for someone who comes mostly from e-commerce, with a stint in drone delivery, how did you end up in SaaS?
zh: 我看了你的背景。你在 Amazon、eBay、Google 工作过,而那个无人机送货业务 Wing 也非常酷。对于一个主要来自电商、又在无人机送货领域待过一阵的人来说,你是怎么进入 SaaS 的?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: I ended up in SaaS completely by accident, because the early days of this started around my time at Fabric. After I left Alphabet and Wing, I joined some ex-colleagues from Staples and eBay who had started a company called Fabric, and I joined as CEO. At that time we were very, very early, still doing our seed round, so I got involved pretty early in the product. The interesting part is we had built something similar at Staples for our e-commerce platform, where we were trying to transition away from the legacy IBM WebSphere. So this became a platform we could serve to everybody that wasn't Amazon, that didn't have all the capabilities Amazon had. That's where my journey into SaaS started. Most of our selling was founder-led selling for SaaS. I took that company from seed to Series C, stayed on the board for a bit soon thereafter, and then joined here. The Irony of the AI Manifesto and the Slop It Produced
zh: 我进入 SaaS 完全是偶然,因为这一切的早期始于我在 Fabric 的时候。离开 Alphabet 和 Wing 之后,我加入了一些来自 Staples 和 eBay 的前同事创立的一家叫 Fabric 的公司,我以 CEO 的身份加入。那时我们非常非常早期,还在做种子轮,所以我很早就参与了产品。有趣的是,我们曾在 Staples 为我们的电商平台构建过类似的东西,当时我们试图从遗留的 IBM WebSphere 迁移出来。所以这成为了一个我们可以服务给所有非 Amazon 的、不具备 Amazon 所有能力的公司的平台。这就是我进入 SaaS 之旅的起点。我们大部分的销售是创始人主导的 SaaS 销售。我把那家公司从种子轮带到了 Series C,之后不久在董事会待了一段时间,然后加入了这里。AI 宣言的讽刺性及其产生的垃圾内容

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: I was going down the rabbit hole on your X profile, and I found a couple of interesting tweets I want to bring up. One was a response to Tobi, co-founder of Shopify. He's all over the place again because he's talking about the AI slop grenade, but he was also the originator of the CEO AI manifesto encouraging people to use AI. And it seems like now people are using AI in ways that aren't very great. So what's your take on that?
zh: 我在你的 X 主页上深入挖掘,发现了几条我想提到的有趣的推文。其中一条是对 Shopify 联合创始人 Tobi 的回复。他现在到处都是,因为他在谈论 AI 垃圾手榴弹,但他也是鼓励人们使用 AI 的 CEO AI 宣言的发起者。而现在看起来人们使用 AI 的方式并不太好。所以你对此怎么看?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: My take, and I wrote about this, is that the FOMO is off the charts. Two years ago it was completely off the charts, and now it's settling down a bit with all the tokens spent. But I always find it's good to be an early adopter, and it's also good to have some data around the adoption, versus just going all-in. The response you're referring to might have been one around the slop grenades he's talking about. The irony I found was: on one hand, we're encouraging everybody that AI will replace every job, don't come to a meeting if you haven't figured it out with AI, and encouraging that as much as possible. And then, on the other hand, talking about how it's just slop central and that's what's happening. With the introduction of AI at work, for those adopting it, it's becoming hard to understand what's actually written by a human versus pure slop. I find it ironic that you can't encourage an organization to go all-in, which is what they did, with no guardrails around it, and then, on the other hand, have a problem with the massive amounts of slop in your organization. You have to pick your lane. Getting Through the Slop to Quality
zh: 我的看法,我写过这方面的东西,是 FOMO(害怕错过)已经爆表了。两年前完全是爆表的,现在随着所有 token 的消耗,它稍微平静了一些。但我总觉得做早期采用者是好事,围绕采用情况拥有一些数据也是好事,而不是直接 all-in。你提到的那条回复可能是关于他谈论的那些垃圾手榴弹的。我发现的讽刺之处是:一方面,我们在鼓励所有人说 AI 将取代每一份工作,如果你还没搞清楚怎么用 AI 就别来开会,并尽可能大力鼓励这一点。然后,另一方面,又在谈论这里简直就是垃圾内容中心,这就是正在发生的事。随着 AI 在工作中的引入,对于那些采用它的人来说,要分辨哪些是真正由人写的、哪些是纯粹的垃圾内容变得越来越难了。我觉得很讽刺的是,你不能鼓励一个组织 all-in——他们就是这么做的——却没有任何护栏,然后,另一方面,又对组织里大量的垃圾内容有意见。你必须选定你的车道。穿越垃圾内容达到质量

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Maybe coming from a startup myself, I also encourage my team to go all-in with AI. And of course, we have to get through slop. I actually had to get through slop in many ways. But I thought of that as a necessary step in order to achieve quality. I wonder if you've found ways to achieve quality without getting through the nitty-gritty of some slop along the way?
zh: 也许我自己来自创业公司,我也鼓励我的团队在 AI 上 all-in。当然,我们必须穿越垃圾内容。实际上我在很多方面都不得不穿越垃圾内容。但我把这看作是达到质量的必要步骤。我想知道你是否找到了不用经历一路上的那些垃圾内容细节就能达到质量的方法?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: AI has a very dominant position in what we do at our enterprise, and even outside a startup environment, AI is really good at the inform and consult part of the equation: getting information so you can consult with it. But what it can't be is completely copy-paste. That's where things get difficult, because human judgment is going to become really important here. If you lack ideas and you're relying heavily on AI for everything, you're not really going to be that important. Nassim Taleb recently tweeted this. I don't know if you follow him, but he said something like, those with high IQ and no original ideas are going to find it very hard in the world of AI. And I tend to agree. You have to be creative at the same time as utilizing AI along the way. So I think you did the right thing, and you probably expected the slop to go up and at some point come back down. I'm still waiting for the come-back-down part.
zh: AI 在我们企业内部所做的事情中占有非常主导的地位,即使在创业公司环境之外,AI 在「告知和咨询」这部分确实非常擅长:获取信息,这样你就可以用它来咨询。但它不能做的就是完全复制粘贴。那是事情变得困难的地方,因为人类判断在这里将变得非常重要。如果你缺乏想法,并且事事都严重依赖 AI,那你其实不会那么重要。Nassim Taleb 最近发了一条推文。我不知道你是否关注他,但他说了类似的话,那些高智商但没有原创想法的人在 AI 的世界里会非常艰难。我倾向于同意这一点。你必须在利用 AI 的同时保持创造力。所以我认为你做了正确的事,你可能预期垃圾内容会先上升,然后在某个时候回落。我还在等待回落的那部分。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: That's true. It's also easy to give up, or to just stay in that slop stage and not push through enough. That's what I found is a lack of, for most of the clients we work with. They're doing all the right things on paper: they send the AI manifesto, they buy the tools, they create some metrics around adoption. But clearly that's not enough.
zh: 确实如此。放弃也容易,或者就停留在垃圾内容阶段而不坚持推进。我发现这正是我们合作的大多数客户所缺乏的。他们在纸面上做着所有正确的事情:他们发布 AI 宣言,他们购买工具,他们围绕采用情况创建一些指标。但显然这还不够。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: I've seen enough tools now flooding the market: knowledge graph this, integrated into all your collaboration tools, getting alerts and alarms through bots powered by the litany of providers. In some cases they're adding more work. They're actually introducing more work into your daily workflow, not deducting it. So where I have a challenge is: AI is not your strategy. It's part of your strategy. It's going to help with your strategy. It cannot become the strategy, because then you've got a problem. It's a tool in the toolkit. It's not going to be the be-all and end-all. Leveraging it in the best way possible while utilizing human judgment, that's where the real impact is. The AI Layer Being Built on Top of SaaS
zh: 我已经见到足够多的工具涌入市场:这个知识图谱、集成到你所有的协作工具里、通过由一长串提供商驱动的机器人发送警报。在某些情况下,它们在增加更多工作。它们实际上是在给你的日常工作流程中引入更多工作,而不是减少。所以我有异议的地方在于:AI 不是你的战略。它是你战略的一部分。它会帮助你的战略。它不能成为战略本身,否则你就有问题了。它是工具箱里的一件工具。它不会是全部和终极。在运用人类判断的同时以最好的方式利用它,那才是真正的影响力所在。构建在 SaaS 之上的 AI 层

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: I want to get your take on this AI layer we're seeing built on top of a lot of SaaS. You come from e-commerce, so you've seen how, now, anyone can throw agents at SaaS to go do things. I've been obsessed with some of these new consumer agents for personal work. So how do you think about that as an actual tool for employee productivity?
zh: 我想听听你对这个我们正看到构建在许多 SaaS 之上的 AI 层的看法。你来自电商,所以你见证了现在任何人都可以把智能体扔到 SaaS 上去做事情。我一直痴迷于一些用于个人工作的新的消费级智能体。那么作为员工生产力的实际工具,你是怎么看待这个的?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: We're on frontier with OpenAI, and it's fairly integrated here at HP with the latest models. To answer your question on some of these consumer agents, you're very courageous to use one, in the sense that you give it all your logins, passwords, and so on. I feel like privacy and security are going to become a big obstacle along the way. It's not going to be trivial to just hand over all your credentials to one bot that's going to go do what it needs to do. People might be very selective about what they use it for. You saw Amazon decline to work with some of these agents, just like the decline with Perplexity. I don't know where I stand on that, because I feel like Amazon's moat is Prime, and customers will continue to go to Amazon because of Prime. They don't need those agents, not today, at least. When it comes to the enterprise, I think Microsoft has done a pretty decent job at this point. The early days were a bit rockier, but with Copilot, the integration of Copilot, and their soon-to-come coworker and Claude for enterprise, I think it's a good product for those who want the capabilities AI can provide alongside their work. The most integrated product right now is probably Microsoft. I don't find that same level of native capabilities out of Google Workspace, at least I haven't seen it there, it's not as integrated. Whereas if you look at Microsoft, Copilot has actually made a lot of gains. HP's Own AI Strategy: Internal Workflows First
zh: 我们是 OpenAI 的前沿合作伙伴,而且它在这里已经与最新模型相当深度地集成在 HP。回答你关于这些消费级智能体的问题,你使用其中一个是非常有勇气的,因为你把所有的登录名、密码等等都交给它。我觉得隐私和安全将会成为这条路上的一个大障碍。把你所有的凭证都交给一个将去做它需要做的事情的机器人,这不会是小事。人们可能会对他们用它做什么非常挑剔。你看到 Amazon 拒绝与一些这样的智能体合作,就像拒绝 Perplexity 那样。我不知道我对此站在哪一边,因为我觉得 Amazon 的护城河是 Prime,客户会继续因为 Prime 去 Amazon。他们不需要那些智能体,至少今天不需要。说到企业,我觉得 Microsoft 在这一点上做得相当不错。早期有点颠簸,但随着 Copilot、Copilot 的集成,以及他们即将推出的 coworker 和 Claude for enterprise,我认为对于那些想要 AI 能力并伴随工作的人来说,这是一个好产品。目前集成度最高的产品可能是 Microsoft。我在 Google Workspace 上没有看到同样程度的原生能力,至少我没在那里看到,它没有那么集成。而如果你看 Microsoft,Copilot 确实取得了很大的进展。HP 自己的 AI 战略:内部工作流先行

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: So where do you play in this arena? You're running the SaaS portfolio for HP, and now you have all of these agent opportunities along the way. So what's your strategy?
zh: 那么你在这个竞技场中扮演什么角色?你在为 HP 运营 SaaS 组合,现在你一路上拥有了所有这些智能体机会。那么你的战略是什么?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Our strategy is for internal workflows. I'm not running IT for the organizations I sell into; I sell into IT leaders. But for our internal organization, the product managers are pushed very hard: what can be done through AI should be done through AI, and what needs a human in the loop, you do that. So the PMs use all the tools available, whether it's the early days of ChatGPT down to Claude now, and wherever they can use tools, they do all that work, from ideation to PRD and beyond. A lot of that is getting heavily compressed. Even early demo videos are so easy now. Everything is just so much easier now, until you need to go to production. That's a whole different ballgame. What we do internally is try to make sure we can leverage as much of the out-of-the-box capabilities Microsoft provides in every facet possible, and then internally accelerate our overall cycle time for getting from ideation all the way to deploying features to the market. Our developers use Codex, Claude Code, and the PMs are all pretty heavy users of AI as well. Pushing Through Enterprise Bureaucracy
zh: 我们的战略是内部工作流。我不是在为我销售的组织运营 IT;我是销售给 IT 领导者。但对于我们的内部组织,产品经理们被 push 得很紧:能通过 AI 完成的就应该通过 AI 完成,而需要人类在环的,你就去做。所以 PM 们使用所有可用的工具,无论是 ChatGPT 的早期直到现在的 Claude,只要能使用工具的地方,他们就做所有那些工作,从构思到 PRD 再往后。其中很多都被大幅压缩了。即使是早期的演示视频现在也非常容易。现在一切都变得容易多了,直到你需要走向生产环境。那完全是另一回事。我们在内部所做的是,尽可能在每个方面利用 Microsoft 提供的开箱即用的能力,然后在内部加速我们整体周期时间,从构思一直到向市场部署功能。我们的开发者使用 Codex、Claude Code,PM 们也都是相当重度的 AI 用户。突破企业官僚主义

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: To what extent, though? In the startup world there's no backup plan, so everybody is forced to move as fast as possible, while in a larger enterprise you can still find ways to slow down. You come from a massive company. Your company is more of a spin-off here, but still it's not small. So how do you push through bureaucracy and other barriers to make sure your PMs can move as fast as possible?
zh: 不过,能在多大程度上做到呢?在创业公司世界里没有备份计划,所以每个人都被迫尽可能快地行动,而在一个更大的企业里,你仍然可以找到放慢速度的办法。你来自一家巨大的公司。你的公司在这里更像是一个分拆,但它仍然不小。那么你如何突破官僚主义和其他障碍,确保你的 PM 们能尽可能快地行动?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Large organizations are about relationships. As much as there's friction to get approvals for certain tools or capabilities, which could be exposure for the organization, you have to build the internal relationships to bring people with you. Early on, back when I joined, Figma was pretty popular, but it wasn't really being utilized much internally. I pushed very hard to make sure that whatever out-of-the-box capabilities Figma provided, we were using for all our design. That's now obviously moved forward to pretty much being able to do everything with the toolset you have internally. I've not seen a ton of challenges outside of the fact that, when you're using a lot of these products, the tokens run out fairly quickly and the budgets are challenging. So that's where it comes down to: where's the ROI for all of this? Because if you can't see the ROI on the amount of money you're spending on those tokens, you have to be able to do the math and be okay with it. When it comes to friction internally, I'd say we haven't faced the level of friction I would assume from a large enterprise like ourselves in utilizing the tools available. Change Has to Come From the Top
zh: 大型组织关乎关系。尽管为某些工具或能力获取审批存在摩擦——这可能是组织的暴露风险——你必须建立内部关系,把人们带到你这一边。早期,在我刚加入的时候,Figma 相当流行,但内部并没有真正被广泛使用。我非常努力地推动,确保 Figma 提供的任何开箱即用的能力,我们都在所有设计中使用。现在这显然已经发展到用你内部拥有的工具集几乎能做所有事情。除了当你使用很多这些产品时,token 消耗得相当快、预算有挑战这一点之外,我没遇到太多挑战。所以这就归结为:这一切的 ROI 在哪里?因为如果你在那些 token 上花的钱看不到 ROI,你必须能够算这笔账并能接受它。说到内部的摩擦,我想说,我们在使用可用工具方面所面临的摩擦,没有达到我原本以为像我们这样的大型企业会有的程度。变革必须自上而下

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: One thing I can imagine from the outside is that a lot of these initiatives at this level have to happen from the very top. Having a leader who is not just talking the talk but walking the walk is necessary. I've seen this so many times with some of our clients: they want to be more AI-native, but they're not really committing to the pain it takes to make it happen. You need someone fighting from the very top, otherwise AI becomes a cute initiative for some people to raise a trophy and say, "I checked my box."
zh: 从外部来看,我能想象的一件事是,这个层面的很多举措必须从最顶层发生。有一位不只是说说而是身体力行的领导者是必要的。我在我们的一些客户身上见过太多次:他们想变得更 AI 原生,但他们并没有真正投入到实现它所需的痛苦之中。你需要有人在最顶层战斗,否则 AI 就会变成某些人举奖杯说「我打卡完成了我那份」的可爱举措。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: I can tell you there was a lot of blood, sweat, and tears going into building the original thesis for Workforce Experience. We're in a business where our platform provides insights on our customers' total surface area: their hardware, software, OS, network, and so on. But at the same time, we also encourage buying less, which is counterproductive to a hardware business, right? So why do we do that? Because ultimately we exist because we want to make that employee experience absolutely world-class. And you can't make a world-class employee experience if you've got a bias in the process. From the top, you have to make sure that bias is removed, and your central focus, your grounding principle, is: how do I improve the experience for the people I'm selling this into? For that, you have to make some trade-offs. To your point, it wasn't easy to convince everybody, but it's less about convincing everyone. It's really important to convince yourself first: Will this work? How relevant is it? Will it have ROI for the people you're selling it into? Is there product-market fit? Is this a plug product, or are you selling it into these people? You have to go through all these questions. Once we found we had PMF, it was all roads leading to "let's go build this faster." Go-to-Market: Selling the Solution, Not the Hardware
zh: 我可以告诉你,构建 Workforce Experience 最初的论点经历了大量的血汗和泪水。我们所在的业务是,我们的平台提供对客户全部覆盖面的洞察:他们的硬件、软件、操作系统、网络等等。但与此同时,我们也鼓励少买,这对硬件业务来说是适得其反的,对吧?那我们为什么这么做?因为归根结底,我们存在是因为我们想让员工体验绝对达到世界级。而如果在这个过程中你有偏向性,你就无法做出世界级的员工体验。从最高层,你必须确保消除偏向,你的核心焦点、你的立足原则是:我如何改善我向其销售这些东西的人的体验?为此,你必须做一些权衡。正如你所说,说服每个人并不容易,但与其说是说服每个人。首先说服你自己真的非常重要:这行得通吗?它的相关性有多大?它对你销售对象会有 ROI 吗?有产品市场契合度吗?这是一个插件式产品,还是你在真正向这些人销售?你必须过一遍所有这些问题。一旦我们发现我们有了 PMF,就是所有道路都通向「让我们更快地构建这个东西」。走向市场:销售解决方案,而不是硬件

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: As you talk about product-market fit, I want to know your go-to-market motion. How much are you leveraging your existing HP relationships to introduce your product, versus going to market directly?
zh: 既然你谈到了产品市场契合度,我想知道你的走向市场动作。你在多大程度上利用现有的 HP 关系来介绍你的产品,而不是直接走向市场?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: We do both. One big friction point early on, although it didn't really become an issue, was when I started pitching Workforce Experience as not a point solution, which we used to have back in the day. Point solutions are interesting, but they're not that relevant to the economic buyer long-term. When you're pitching a platform, the platform has to be completely agnostic of your own stuff that's involved in it. So we went device-agnostic and OS-agnostic. We didn't care if the fleets we were selling into were competitors' brands or a completely different OS. Our principled approach was: we don't care what hardware you're running, we want to make sure we can help you run that environment better. Once you have those very specific principles outlined on why you're doing that, and people are on board, it becomes a lot easier to move forward. On how we do the go-to-market: we rely heavily on our existing go-to-market rails. As a very large hardware seller, an OEM, we are constantly in conversations where our account reps are dealing with customers who are buying competitor product. In the past, HP used to sell third-party software. We don't do that anymore. All the IP we've built, we're selling as our own software. So the transition was basically: we're not going to do that anymore, we're going to sell our own home-built, owned-IP product. In those conversations, what's evolved now is that instead of selling hardware, we're selling the solution: what problem are you trying to solve? Our go-to-market relies heavily on CIOs and RFPs coming in with explanations around "we're trying to solve this problem," and Workforce Experience fits into that, versus selling the software with the hardware, which just doesn't scale. How Close Are You to the Outcome?
zh: 我们两者都做。早期一个大的摩擦点——虽然它最终没真正成为问题——是当我开始推销 Workforce Experience 时,不是作为一个单点解决方案,而我们过去是那种。单点解决方案有趣,但它们对经济买家长期而言没那么相关。当你在推销一个平台时,这个平台必须对你自身参与其中的东西完全不可知。所以我们做到了设备无关和操作系统无关。我们不在乎我们销售的舰队是竞争对手的品牌还是完全不同的操作系统。我们的原则性方法是:我们不在乎你运行什么硬件,我们想确保能帮助你更好地运行那个环境。一旦你把做这些的非常具体的原则阐述清楚,并且人们认同了,前进就变得容易得多。关于我们如何做走向市场:我们严重依赖我们现有的走向市场轨道。作为一个非常大的硬件销售商、一个 OEM,我们不断处于这样的对话中:我们的客户经理正在与购买竞争对手产品的客户打交道。过去,HP 曾销售第三方软件。我们不再那样做了。我们构建的所有 IP,我们都作为自己的软件来销售。所以转变基本上是:我们不再那样做了,我们要销售自己自研的、自有 IP 的产品。在这些对话中,现在演变的是:我们不再销售硬件,而是销售解决方案:你想解决什么问题?我们的走向市场严重依赖 CIO 和带着「我们想解决这个问题」说明而来的 RFP,而 Workforce Experience 契合其中,而不是把软件和硬件捆绑销售,那根本无法规模化。你离结果有多近?

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: The million-dollar question for a lot of the CIOs being pitched software, hardware, hybrid solutions is: how close are you to the outcome, versus just telling me that with this new software my employees are going to increase productivity by X percent?
zh: 对于许多被推销软件、硬件、混合解决方案的 CIO 来说,那个价值百万美元的问题是:你离结果有多近,而不只是告诉我有了这个新软件我的员工生产力会提高百分之多少?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: We're very clear on that, because when we started dogfooding the product inside HP, it wasn't a low bar. It was a high bar to convince our own IT teams to use it. We had 80,000 devices and hundreds, if not thousands, of pieces of software running in these environments. We had to convince our internal teams that this is the path forward and it will help them manage HP's IT environment better. Not until we crossed that threshold and accomplished some success there did we even go to market. So we had a very long alpha, a pretty long beta, then an extended release. We didn't go GA for a long time, and at every stage we had 15 to 20 to 100 partners alongside us looking at the ROI of what we deliver. An example: we're not walking into our customers' offices saying, "buy this and we'll promise you the world and nothing will happen on the other side." We're actually telling them their ticket volume will go down by 30 to 40%, because Workforce Experience will tackle all those tickets behind the scenes. That's pure ROI, because all those tickets are managed by desk-side support. One ticket is, I don't know, six, ten, twenty dollars, whatever it takes to resolve, and it's a headache for the employee. Second, we have a feature called Smart Refresh, which evaluates all your fleet and says what you should not be buying. In the IT industry, what ends up happening is hardware is bought on 3-to-4-year cycles, in a really monolithic process: "it's done this way, so that's the way we'll do it again, let's go buy 100,000 machines." We're breaking that mold and saying, actually, no, you shouldn't be buying 100,000 machines. You should be buying 55,000 machines, upgrade these, and Workforce Experience can manage all the others in a perfect configuration, so you can extend the life of your machine. That comes at a very low cost to them, because we can manage all of it. But think about that for a second: nobody else is doing that.
zh: 我们在这点上非常清楚,因为当我们开始在 HP 内部内部使用这个产品时,标准并不低。说服我们自己的 IT 团队使用它是一个很高的门槛。我们有 80,000 台设备和数百甚至数千个软件在这些环境中运行。我们必须说服我们的内部团队,这是前进的道路,它会帮助他们更好地管理 HP 的 IT 环境。直到我们跨过那个门槛并在那里取得一些成功,我们才走向市场。所以我们有一个非常长的 alpha,一个相当长的 beta,然后是延长的发布。我们很长时间没有 GA,在每个阶段我们都有 15 到 20 到 100 个合作伙伴伴随我们,审视我们交付的 ROI。举个例子:我们不是走进客户的办公室说「买这个,我们向你承诺全世界,然后另一方什么都不会发生」。我们实际上是在告诉他们他们的工单量会下降 30% 到 40%,因为 Workforce Experience 会在幕后处理所有那些工单。那是纯粹的 ROI,因为所有那些工单都是由桌面支持来处理的。一张工单,我不知道,六块、十块、二十美元,不管解决它需要多少,而且对员工来说是个头疼事。其次,我们有一个叫 Smart Refresh 的功能,它评估你的整个舰队,并告诉你不应该买什么。在 IT 行业,最终发生的事情是硬件按 3 到 4 年的周期购买,以一种非常僵化的流程:「以前是这么做的,所以我们再这么做一次,让我们去买 100,000 台机器。」我们正在打破那个模式,说,实际上,不,你不应该买 100,000 台机器。你应该买 55,000 台机器,升级这些,而 Workforce Experience 可以用完美的配置管理所有其他的,这样你就能延长机器的寿命。这对他们来说成本非常低,因为我们可以管理全部。但想一想这一点:没有其他人在做这件事。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: As an executive myself, that's what I need to hear. How is this solution going to make me more money, or save me some cost? Everything in between is kind of unclear.
zh: 作为一个高管,这正是我需要听到的。这个解决方案将如何让我赚更多的钱,或帮我省下一些成本?中间的一切都 kinda 不清楚。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: If we can't provide that return on their investment, we shouldn't exist. It's as simple as that. The right to be in the room is only allowed until we can demonstrate the performance. We've had partners come back and tell us that not only has their ticket volume gone down, their mean average time to resolve tickets has gone down by 30%. So what used to take six or seven days is now taking two or three days. Those are the types of things we love hearing. We saw that when folks are refreshing their fleets, they're spending 20, 30 million, and they're spending 25 to 30% less. In the end, that's all cash. That's all cash leaving their enterprise. If Workforce Experience can help you with that, isn't that what you want? You want to reduce costs, be more secure, and have higher velocity in your IT environment. What AI Does to the Management Layer
zh: 如果我们不能为他们的投资提供回报,我们就不应该存在。就这么简单。待在房间里的权利,只有在我们能证明绩效的时候才被允许。我们有合作伙伴回来告诉我们,不仅他们的工单量下降了,他们解决工单的平均时间也下降了 30%。所以过去需要六七天的事情,现在只需要两三天。这些就是我们所爱听到的那类事情。我们看到,当人们刷新他们的舰队时,他们花费两三千万,而他们少花了 25% 到 30%。归根结底,那都是现金。那都是离开他们企业的现金。如果 Workforce Experience 能在这方面帮助你,这不正是你想要的吗?你想降低成本、更安全,并在你的 IT 环境中有更高的速度。AI 对管理层做了什么

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: You have a front-row seat to workforce transformation. You're seeing companies go up and down in headcount, especially now with AI. So I'm really curious: what do you think is going to happen in the midterm due to the AI impact on business?
zh: 你在劳动力转型方面有一线视角。你看到公司的员工人数起起伏伏,尤其是现在有了 AI。所以我真的很好奇:你认为在中期内,AI 对商业的影响会发生什么?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: I mentioned this in a previous podcast, about the layers. What AI is demonstrably doing immediately is that those additional layers of management are just not that necessary anymore. Longer-term, because a lot of that monitoring, management, data collection, and aggregation of information can be done by individuals, if you have to rely on a manager reporting to a manager reporting to a director, I'm not sure all those layers scale long-term with AI, because AI can do a lot of that work. That's one. Second, we're seeing a lot of requests, and we've built a new alpha in our labs, a product called AI Command Center. So when you buy Workforce Experience in the future, there's a capability that comes with our elite package that will look at your entire landscape of employees and their AI adoption, usage, and yield. We can actually help you predict and manage not just your budgeting, but also how your employees are adopting all the technology you're releasing to them. That's something we're hearing a lot more about: how can I make sure my employees are more efficient at what they do? The challenge has been that most of these CIOs haven't seen the return from all of these things, and we want to give them a clear, visible line of sight: here are the employees by department, by persona, by usage, using these models. How can you make them more efficient? How can you make sure there's adoption in the right places? That's what people are looking for. Ultimately, to your question, you'll still have people in these organizations, but fundamentally, managers will have to know a lot more than just managing. Who Manages the Fleet of Agents?
zh: 我在之前的一个播客里提到过这一点,关于层级。AI 立刻能证明在做的是,那些额外的管理层已经不那么必要了。更长期来看,因为很多那些监督、管理、数据收集和信息聚合都可以由个人完成,如果你必须依赖一个经理向一个经理汇报再向一个总监汇报,我不确定所有这些层级能否与 AI 长期共存,因为 AI 可以做其中很多工作。这是第一点。第二,我们看到很多需求,我们在实验室里构建了一个新的 alpha,一个叫 AI Command Center 的产品。所以未来当你购买 Workforce Experience 时,我们的精英套餐会附带一项能力,它会审视你的整个员工图景以及他们的 AI 采用、使用和产出。我们实际上可以帮你预测和管理,不仅是你的预算,还有你的员工对你发布给他们的所有技术的采用情况。这是我们听到越来越多的事情:我如何确保我的员工在他们的工作中更高效?挑战在于,大多数这些 CIO 还没有从所有这些东西中看到回报,而我们想给他们一条清晰可见的视线:这里是按部门、按角色、按使用情况划分的、正在使用这些模型的员工。你如何让他们更高效?你如何确保在正确的地方有采用?这就是人们在寻找的。归根结底,回到你的问题,这些组织中仍然会有人,但从根本上说,管理者将必须知道的远不止管理本身。谁来管理智能体舰队?

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: That's a real challenge right now. In my case, we're deploying a bunch of agents, obsessing over it, really finding ways to use AI instead of a human when we have a problem. But the problem we're creating on the back end is: who's going to manage this fleet of agents? How good are they? When do we actually need a human instead of an agent, or a combination? I still haven't seen a way to easily manage that type of relationship.
zh: 这是现在一个真正的挑战。以我为例,我们正在部署一大堆智能体,为之痴迷,真正寻找在我们有问题时用 AI 代替人类的方法。但我们在后端正在制造的问题是:谁来管理这支智能体舰队?它们有多好?我们什么时候真正需要人类而不是智能体,或者两者的组合?我仍然没有看到一个能轻松管理这种类型关系的方法。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: It's not a trivial one to manage, because, back to your earlier point, agents just talking to agents all day long, I'm not sure. Ultimately, someone has to make a decision. When it's a higher-fidelity decision, there's going to be a human involved, because agents are not going to have responsibility for those. So I could envision a place, in the retail arena for example, where a traditional retailer has a buyer, a planner, and a merchandiser who does all the marketing activity, and they'd all have assistants next to them: an assistant buyer, a planner level one, a site merchandiser level one, with AI. I think those second levels are agents, and those first-level buyers are now not managers. They're actually ICs managing agents. That's the format I see. What is a buyer in e-commerce ultimately doing all day? They're negotiating prices, submitting POs, selecting product, selecting vendors. Those tasks don't seem, in the world of these new AI agents, like they can't be done by AI. So the flip is: where you were a manager, one could foresee that now you're managing the agents. What Fewer Human Seats Means for Pricing
zh: 管理起来不是一件小事,因为,回到你之前的观点,智能体整天互相交谈,我不确定。归根结底,必须有人做决定。当它是一个更高保真度的决定时,会有一个人参与,因为智能体不会对这些承担负责。所以我可以设想一个场景,例如在零售领域,一个传统零售商有一个买手、一个计划员和一个做所有营销活动的商品专员,他们旁边都会有助手:一个助手买手、一个一级计划员、一个一级网站商品专员,都带着 AI。我认为那些第二层级是智能体,而那些一级买手现在不是管理者。他们实际上是管理智能体的 IC。这就是我看到的形态。一个电商买手整天到底在做什么?他们在谈判价格、提交 PO、挑选产品、挑选供应商。在这个新 AI 智能体的世界里,这些任务看起来并非不能由 AI 完成。所以反转是:你曾经是一个管理者,可以预见现在你是在管理智能体。更少的人类席位对定价意味着什么

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: Back to your current business: how does that impact your pricing model? Traditional SaaS bases pricing on seats, and now you have fewer human seats. So what does that mean for you?
zh: 回到你目前的业务:这如何影响你的定价模式?传统 SaaS 基于席位定价,而现在你的人类席位更少了。那对你意味着什么?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Fewer human seats is totally fine by us, because ultimately we're committing to ROI around your spend and your overall ticketing volume: how much are you spending on desk-side support? That's a pretty large expense for large enterprises to manage 24/7. We see a world where those seats could exist and not exist, but move to more of a rev-share model or a cost-reduction model. In the future state, we can imagine a world where you had X number of tickets a year, we commit to this much reduction overall, and based on that, we charge you a fee that's outcome-based. That doesn't seem out of scope, because CIOs are getting smarter about not just paying for dashboards that aren't useful. They're paying for actual outcomes. So I see a clear path: you can be either seat-based with commitments on outcomes, or purely outcome-based. The skin in the game with the outcome-based model makes the equation very equal. It's a win for you and a win for us. The best negotiations in the world are when both parties are winning. If one party is losing, the deal doesn't work out that well long-term; it's really good short-term, you can high-five all day long, but a year later you're churning that customer. So what AI is doing is a bit of a leveling of the playing field: do I need all these pieces of software? What are they doing for me? Are they actually generating ROI? Is there a way to compute that? If there isn't, I don't need it. I kind of like that, because we believe that if it were just a software business not supporting the hardware business, there are so many of those, but we have a unique position.
zh: 更少的人类席位对我们来说完全没问题,因为归根结底,我们承诺的是围绕你的支出和你整体工单量的 ROI:你在桌面支持上花费多少?对大型企业来说,管理 24/7 的桌面支持是一笔相当大的开支。我们看到一个世界,那些席位可能存在也可能不存在,但会转向更多分成模式或降本模式。在未来状态,我们可以想象一个世界,你每年有 X 数量的工单,我们承诺整体减少这么多,基于此,我们向你收取一笔基于结果的费用。这看起来并不超出范围,因为 CIO 们正变得更聪明,不再只是为没用的仪表板付费。他们为实际结果付费。所以我看到一条清晰的路径:你可以是基于席位但有结果承诺的,也可以是纯基于结果的。基于结果模式下的利益绑定让这个等式非常平等。对你是个胜利,对我们也是个胜利。世界上最好的谈判是双方都在赢的时候。如果一方在输,这笔交易长期就不会太好;短期真的很好,你可以整天击掌,但一年后你就在流失那个客户了。所以 AI 正在做的是一种拉平竞争环境:我需要所有这些软件吗?它们在为我做什么?它们真的在产生 ROI 吗?有没有办法计算它?如果没有,我就不需要它。我 kinda 喜欢这样,因为我们相信,如果只是一个不支持硬件业务的软件业务,那样的公司太多了,但我们有一个独特的位置。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: We have some extreme examples already in the market, not a lot. A helpdesk platform, for example, just got acquired by Salesforce for $3.6 billion, I believe, and it's all about outcome-based pricing, some number of dollars per ticket resolved. I think the closer we can get our pricing to the outcome of the client, the better for both. It puts extra pressure on the vendor to actually deliver on what they promised, but it's actually a good thing.
zh: 我们在市场上已经有一些极端的例子,不多。比如一个帮助台平台,我相信刚被 Salesforce 以 36 亿美元收购,它就是基于结果的定价,每解决一张工单收一定数额的钱。我认为我们能越接近客户的成果来定价,对双方都越好。这给供应商带来了兑现承诺的额外压力,但实际上是件好事。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: At some point, why do you want anything inside your IT environment if it's not accretive to the bottom line of what you do? What's the purpose? Just for pretty dashboards? That's meaningless. Staying Close to the Work as an Executive
zh: 到某个时候,如果对你的 IT 环境中的任何东西都不利于你的底线,你为什么还要它?目的是什么?就为了好看的仪表板?那毫无意义。作为高管保持贴近一线工作

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: No more dashboards, please. I'm burning dashboards. I don't want more meetings for the sake of meetings. It's been liberating to know I can do a lot of things myself again, like when we were much smaller. It's huge. So I'm curious how that applies at the scale you operate at. You're the President of HP Digital Services, but you're still very in tune with what's going on in the market. What are some of the pockets where you still want to feel a bit more like an IC?
zh: 请不要再有仪表板了。我正在烧掉仪表板。我不想要更多为了开会而开的会。知道我又能自己做很多事情了,就像我们规模还小得多的时候那样,这很解放。这太重要了。所以我很好奇这在你运营的规模上如何适用。你是 HP Digital Services 的总裁,但你仍然非常了解市场上正在发生什么。有哪些方面你仍然想感觉更像一个 IC?

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: I feel fairly liberated with AI, because a lot of the long-tail tasks are being managed through AI. I have an agent that runs overnight and looks at what's really important to me, with pre-drafts ready. I'm doing all the stuff you're probably doing, and everybody in a similar job to mine is probably doing. The usage of AI for executives is very different from the usage of AI for ICs. Let's be clear about this: when you're an executive, you've got a support structure around you that eliminates the need for too much AI, because you've got human beings around you. But where you do need AI, it's there. Where I feel more liberated is that I want to spend as much time as possible with customers, and with existing customers versus new customers. That's number one, because I believe existing customers are more important than new customers. They trusted you, they brought you in, and you have to do everything possible to build a repeatable, predictable product that has ROI. Number two, this AI Command Center I talked about, I'm personally involved in architecting what we're building, and I find that so amazing, because I'm able to be in a room with the PMs and the engineering teams tackling issues like: where's that data going to come from? What are we going to do about this? How are we looking at synthetic data versus real data? How are we going to surface this, and what action are customers going to take? I love that part, because it gets your juices going, to really think about what the ultimate goal is and how we get there. Longer-term, for us, selling more hardware is not the answer. It's selling more actual value to the customer. That could come in a SaaS product combined with hardware, or either or, but it ultimately has to be measurable. So I'm spending a lot more time with upcoming product labs and customers.
zh: 我觉得有了 AI 相当解放,因为很多长尾任务正在通过 AI 管理。我有一个智能体在夜间运行,审视什么对我来说真正重要,并准备好预先草稿。我在做你可能在做的事情,每一个和我类似工作的人可能都在做的事情。AI 对高管的使用与 AI 对 IC 的使用非常不同。让我们把这点说清楚:当你是一个高管时,你身边有一个支持结构,消除了对太多 AI 的需求,因为你身边有人类。但在你需要 AI 的地方,它就在那里。我感到更解放的地方是,我想尽可能多地花时间与客户在一起,是与现有客户而不是新客户。这是第一,因为我相信现有客户比新客户更重要。他们信任你,他们把你带了进来,你必须尽一切可能构建一个可重复、可预测、有 ROI 的产品。第二,我谈到的这个 AI Command Center,我亲自参与构建它的架构,我发现这太棒了,因为我能和 PM 和工程团队坐在一个房间里解决这样的问题:那些数据将从哪里来?我们要怎么处理这个?我们如何看待合成数据与真实数据?我们要如何呈现它,客户会采取什么行动?我爱这部分,因为它让你热血沸腾,去真正思考最终目标是什么以及我们如何到达那里。更长期来看,对我们而言,销售更多硬件不是答案。是向客户销售更多实际价值。这可能来自一个与硬件结合的 SaaS 产品,或者两者任一,但它最终必须是可衡量的。所以我花更多时间与即将上线的产品实验室和客户在一起。

speaker: Carlos González de Villaumbrosia
en: It's been awesome to connect with you and learn from your experience at a pretty large organization that's operating in a pretty AI-native way. Thank you for your time.
zh: 能与你交流并从一个以相当 AI 原生的方式运营的相当大的组织中学习你的经验,真是太棒了。感谢你的时间。

speaker: Faisal Masud
en: Thank you, and thanks for some great questions.
zh: 谢谢,也谢谢这些精彩的问题。
